:::{#def-code}
#### Binary code and expected length

Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with probability mass function $p(x) \eqdef \P(X=x)$.
A **binary code** for $X$ assigns each value $x$ a *codeword*,
a finite string of binary digits, of length $\ell(x)$.
The code is **uniquely decodable**
if every finite sequence of codewords, written one after another,
can be split back into codewords in only one way.
The **expected length** of the code is

$$L \eqdef \E{\ell(X)} = \sum_{x} p(x) \, \ell(x).$$

:::
